internship.title: Java Web Development Internship
internship.description: An industry-oriented Java web engineering internship that progresses from HTTP, Spring MVC, Maven, and dependency injection into validated web features, PostgreSQL/JPA persistence, transactions, Spring Security, testing, debugging, observability, delivery, performance reasoning, and maintainability. The final assessment is one complete secure issue-tracking web application with file-wise implementation, schema migration, tests, operational health, and deployment guidance.
prerequisites: Java fundamentals: classes, interfaces, collections, exceptions, and basic OOP.
Basic HTTP methods, status codes, headers, and JSON.
Ability to install and run JDK 25 and Maven.
objectives: Build Spring Boot web applications with Spring MVC.
Design REST APIs and server-rendered views.
Persist relational data using PostgreSQL and Spring Data JPA.
Use transactions, pagination, indexing, and query-plan analysis.
Implement authentication, authorization, secure password storage, and browser security controls.
Debug failures using evidence and produce regression coverage.
Apply Maven, Git, documentation, health checks, container, CI/CD, and rollback concepts.

competencies.name: Java web implementation
competencies.evidence: Controllers, services, persistence, views, and security in the capstone.

competencies.name: API design
competencies.evidence: Methods, statuses, DTOs, validation, pagination and errors.

competencies.name: Database engineering
competencies.evidence: JPA, PostgreSQL constraints, transactions, migration, indexes and query plans.

competencies.name: Security
competencies.evidence: Authentication, authorization, PasswordEncoder, CSRF/session controls, OWASP review.

competencies.name: Testing/debugging
competencies.evidence: JUnit/MVC tests, integration strategy, regression workflow.

competencies.name: Engineering practice
competencies.evidence: Maven lifecycle, Git workflow, documentation, observability, delivery.

phases.title: Foundation
phases.outcome: Runnable MVC service and Maven workflow

modules.title: Java Web Foundations and Tooling
modules.description: Learn HTTP, Spring MVC, Maven, dependency injection, and maintainable boundaries.

lessons.title: HTTP and the Java Web Request Lifecycle
lessons.description: Trace how a browser or API client reaches a Java web application and how Spring MVC dispatches the request.
learningObjectives: trace a request through the servlet container and DispatcherServlet
identify the boundaries between transport and application logic

notes.text: The request path

A servlet container accepts HTTP traffic and invokes the application. In Spring MVC, DispatcherServlet acts as the front controller and coordinates handler mapping, argument binding, message conversion, and response handling.

items: HTTP is a protocol contract; Java code implements application behavior behind that contract.
Controllers should remain focused on translating HTTP concerns.
Services should own business operations and repositories should isolate persistence.

practicals.title: Request Trace with curl
practicals.description: Build and inspect a minimal GET endpoint.
steps: Create a controller mapped to GET /api/ping.
Call it with curl and inspect status and body.
practicals.output: The client receives an HTTP 200 response with a small JSON body.

quiz.question: Which Spring MVC component acts as the front controller?
quiz.explanation: DispatcherServlet coordinates Spring MVC request dispatch.

summary: A web request crosses multiple layers; understanding those layers prevents misplaced logic and makes debugging systematic.

lessons.title: RESTful Endpoint Design and HTTP Semantics
lessons.description: Design resource-oriented endpoints using appropriate methods, status codes, and JSON contracts.
learningObjectives: select HTTP methods for common operations
choose appropriate success and error status codes
define predictable request and response representations

notes.text: Contract first
API consumers should not need to infer success from free-form text. Status codes, JSON shape, validation rules, pagination semantics, and authorization expectations form the contract.

items: GET is intended to be safe; PUT has idempotent semantics; POST is not inherently idempotent.
201 Created communicates successful creation; 204 No Content communicates success without a response body.
Do not use 200 for every outcome just because a framework allows it.

quiz.question: Which status normally communicates that POST created a new resource?
quiz.explanation: 201 Created explicitly communicates successful resource creation.

summary: HTTP semantics are part of the API design and should be tested like any other interface.

lessons.title: Maven Build Lifecycle and Dependency Management
lessons.description: Use Maven to build a reproducible Java application and understand the lifecycle phases that support team development.
learningObjectives: keep generated artifacts out of source control

notes.text: Lifecycle
Maven defines a standard build lifecycle. The validate, compile, test, package, verify, install, and deploy phases provide predictable stages that tooling and CI systems can invoke consistently.

mvn clean test
mvn verify
mvn spring-boot:run

quiz.question: Which Maven phase executes tests before packaging?
quiz.explanation: The test phase runs the project tests.

summary: A predictable build is a prerequisite for code review and automated delivery.

lessons.title: Dependency Injection and Application Layering
lessons.description: Design controllers, services, repositories, and DTOs with explicit responsibilities and testable dependencies.
learningObjectives: separate transport, business, and persistence responsibilities
use constructor injection for required collaborators

notes.text: Responsibilities

items: Controller: HTTP binding, status codes, request/response translation.
Service: business operations and transaction boundaries.
Repository: persistence access.
DTO: external contract.

quiz.question: Where should domain/business rules normally live in a layered Spring application?
quiz.explanation: The service layer is a natural boundary for business operations.

summary: Explicit dependencies make classes easier to reason about and test independently.

tasks.title: Create a Reproducible Spring MVC Skeleton
tasks.description: Build the smallest useful Java web service and document its build workflow.
tasks.problemStatement: Provide a /api/ping endpoint that builds and runs through Maven.
constraints: No database or security configuration is required.
tasks.hint: Use the standard Maven layout and spring-boot-starter-webmvc.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The application entry point starts Spring Boot, while the controller maps the HTTP GET path and serializes the returned map as JSON. In a real project the controller should be a separate file.

modules.title: Web Features and Validation
modules.description: Build validated APIs, predictable errors, and server-rendered views.

lessons.title: Externalized Configuration and Profiles
lessons.description: Separate environment-specific settings from application code and keep secrets out of repositories.
learningObjectives: use configuration properties and environment variables

notes.text: Runtime configuration
Do not commit passwords, API keys, or private keys to Git. Configuration belongs in the environment or an appropriate secret-management system.

quiz.question: Where should production database credentials be supplied?
quiz.explanation: Secrets should not be stored in source control.

summary: The same artifact can move between environments when configuration is externalized.

lessons.title: DTOs and Bean Validation
lessons.description: Build explicit request objects and reject malformed input at the web boundary.
learningObjectives: distinguish validation failures from business-rule failures

notes.text: Boundary validation

items: DTOs keep API contracts separate from persistence entities.
Validation catches malformed input early.
Business rules that depend on stored state belong in application logic.

practicals.title: Validated Issue Creation
practicals.description: Reject invalid issue input at the web boundary.
steps: Add an MVC test that expects 400.
practicals.output: Invalid requests are rejected before business processing.

quiz.question: Which constraint rejects an empty or whitespace-only title?
quiz.explanation: @NotBlank requires non-whitespace content.

summary: Validation is a security and quality boundary because every external request is untrusted.

lessons.title: Centralized REST Error Handling
lessons.description: Return useful, stable error responses without exposing internal implementation details.
learningObjectives: map domain exceptions to status codes
avoid leaking stack traces and infrastructure details

notes.text: Error contract
Do not expose SQL, stack traces, file-system paths, framework internals, or secrets in client-facing errors.

quiz.question: Which annotation is designed for centralized REST exception handling?
quiz.explanation: It centralizes controller exception handling and response mapping.

summary: Centralized errors let controllers focus on happy-path orchestration and keep the error contract consistent.

lessons.title: Server-Side HTML with Thymeleaf
lessons.description: Render a maintainable server-side web page and understand safe data binding.
learningObjectives: keep business logic out of templates

notes.text: MVC view flow
Use templates for presentation. Keep authorization decisions, database access, and business calculations in application code.

quiz.question: What does a controller commonly return to select a Thymeleaf view?
quiz.explanation: A logical view name is resolved to the configured template.

summary: Server-rendered pages are one valid Java web architecture and can coexist with JSON endpoints.

tasks.title: Add Validated Issue Input
tasks.description: Protect an issue-creation endpoint from malformed data.
tasks.problemStatement: Reject a blank title and oversize title before the service is invoked.
constraints: Do not rely on browser-only validation.
tasks.hint: Put transport constraints directly on the request record.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The record is the transport contract. Bean Validation rejects malformed values before the service write path.

modules.title: Persistence and Database Engineering
modules.description: Map relational state with JPA and reason about transaction and query performance.

lessons.title: JPA Entities and Relational Modeling
lessons.description: Map a small issue-tracking domain to PostgreSQL using explicit relational constraints.

notes.text: Persistence model
Do not use entity objects as public API contracts when their shape or relationships can disclose internal details.

quiz.question: Which annotation identifies a JPA persistence entity?
quiz.explanation: @Entity marks a class as a persistent entity.

summary: Entity mapping connects object state to a relational model; the schema remains the source of database integrity.

lessons.title: Spring Data JPA Repositories
lessons.description: Use repository abstractions for common access patterns and keep query intent explicit.
learningObjectives: recognize when explicit queries or projections are better

items: Repository abstractions reduce repetitive data-access code.
Pagination belongs close to the data-access boundary for large collections.
Measure before adding indexes or complex query rewrites.

quiz.question: Which interface provides JPA repository CRUD operations?
quiz.explanation: JpaRepository provides Spring Data JPA repository operations.

summary: Spring Data JPA provides a consistent repository programming model while retaining JPA semantics.

lessons.title: Transactions and Consistency
lessons.description: Choose transaction boundaries around business operations that must be consistent.
learningObjectives: distinguish database transactions from distributed operations

notes.text: Transaction boundary
A database transaction does not make a remote HTTP call atomic with the database.

quiz.question: Which annotation declares a Spring transaction boundary?
quiz.explanation: @Transactional defines transaction semantics for a Spring-managed operation.

summary: Use transactions to protect data consistency without holding them open across unrelated slow operations.

lessons.title: Pagination, Indexes, and EXPLAIN
lessons.description: Bound database work and use PostgreSQL query plans for evidence-based optimization.

notes.text: Bounded reads

CREATE INDEX idx_issues_status_created_at
ON issues (status, created_at DESC);

EXPLAIN ANALYZE
SELECT id, title, created_at
FROM issues
WHERE status = 'OPEN'
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 20;
Indexes can accelerate reads when they match query patterns but have storage and write-maintenance costs. Query plans provide evidence for decisions.

practicals.title: Index a Query Pattern
practicals.description: Create an index aligned with status filtering and created_at ordering.
steps: Add the index to a Flyway migration.
Run the query with EXPLAIN ANALYZE.
Compare plan behavior before and after on representative data.
practicals.solution:
CREATE INDEX idx_issues_status_created_at
ON issues (status, created_at DESC);
practicals.output: The index exists; actual speedup must be measured on the target dataset.

quiz.question: Why should a list endpoint paginate potentially large data sets?
quiz.explanation: Pagination bounds database, memory, and network work per request.

summary: Performance work should start from bounded operations and measured evidence.

tasks.title: Model PostgreSQL Persistence
tasks.description: Create a relational issue model and repository.
tasks.problemStatement: Persist an Issue with explicit status, priority, timestamps, and a creator relationship.
constraints: Keep DTOs separate from entity JSON.
tasks.hint: Write down database invariants before mapping them.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The entity maps durable issue state. Database constraints should enforce required fields, while repositories supply access patterns.

modules.title: Spring Security and Secure Web Design
modules.description: Implement authentication, authorization, password protection, session security, and risk review.

lessons.title: Authentication and Authorization
lessons.description: Implement identity verification and server-side permission checks with Spring Security.
learningObjectives: protect destructive operations at the server

notes.text: Two questions
Authentication verifies who a user is. Authorization determines what that identity may do. Hiding buttons in a browser does not enforce access control; the server must enforce it.

practicals.title: Protect Administrative Delete
practicals.description: Enforce ADMIN-only deletion on the server.
practicals.output: A USER is denied while an authorized ADMIN may delete.

quiz.question: Which statement is correct?
options: Authentication verifies identity; authorization checks permissions
Authentication checks permissions; authorization verifies identity
quiz.answer: Authentication verifies identity; authorization checks permissions
quiz.explanation: The mechanisms solve different security questions.

summary: Authorization must be enforced at the operation boundary, not just in UI code.

lessons.title: Password Storage
lessons.description: Handle user passwords using framework-supported password hashing rather than plaintext or fast hashes.
learningObjectives: avoid exposing or logging credential material

notes.text: Never store plaintext passwords. A password storage function should be deliberately slow and salted; do not substitute a fast general-purpose hash such as SHA-256 alone.

quiz.question: What should an application persist for a password?
quiz.explanation: Password verification should use a password-hashing strategy.

summary: Credential storage is a specialized security problem; use established framework primitives rather than inventing a scheme.

lessons.title: CSRF, Sessions, and Cookies
lessons.description: Understand browser credential behavior and use secure session practices for server-rendered applications.
learningObjectives: distinguish stateful browser sessions from stateless APIs

notes.text: Browser threat model

CSRF abuses a user's browser sending ambient credentials to a trusted site. Spring Security provides CSRF protection for common servlet applications by default. Cookie attributes can reduce exposure: HttpOnly blocks ordinary script access, Secure limits sending to HTTPS, and SameSite constrains cross-site sending.
Do not store session IDs or long-lived authentication credentials in localStorage simply because JavaScript can access them.

quiz.question: Which cookie attribute prevents normal JavaScript from reading its value?
quiz.explanation: HttpOnly limits access through the browser's script-facing cookie APIs.

summary: Browser authentication security includes both server-side session policy and browser-enforced cookie behavior.

lessons.title: OWASP-Oriented Secure Design Review
lessons.description: Use the current OWASP Top 10 as a lens for reviewing a Java web application's common risk categories.
learningObjectives: map common risks to concrete controls

notes.text: OWASP Top 10:2025

The 2025 OWASP Top 10 lists Broken Access Control, Security Misconfiguration, Software Supply Chain Failures, Cryptographic Failures, Injection, Insecure Design, Authentication Failures, Software or Data Integrity Failures, Security Logging & Alerting Failures, and Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions.

items: Prefer parameterized access patterns instead of building SQL from request strings.
Treat authorization as a server-side invariant.
Review dependencies and build inputs as part of the software supply chain.

quiz.question: Which OWASP 2025 category covers missing or bypassable permission checks?
quiz.explanation: A01 focuses on broken authorization and access boundaries.

summary: Security review should connect risks to specific controls and tests rather than stopping at a checklist.

tasks.title: Enforce ADMIN Authorization
tasks.description: Protect destructive operations with server-side authorization.
tasks.problemStatement: A USER must receive an authorization failure while an ADMIN is allowed to delete.
constraints: Do not enforce permissions only in the UI.
tasks.hint: Use method security at the operation boundary.
tasks.solutionExplanation: Request authorization requires identity while method authorization adds a business-operation permission check. PasswordEncoder protects stored credentials.

modules.assessment: Show that unauthorized deletion is denied.

modules.title: Testing, Integration, and Debugging
modules.description: Develop reliable software with unit tests, MVC tests, realistic integration testing, and regression analysis.

lessons.title: JUnit 5 Unit Testing
lessons.description: Write focused unit tests for service behavior with JUnit Jupiter and Mockito.

notes.text: Fast unit tests form the inner feedback loop. Do not mock every object indiscriminately; mock infrastructure boundaries when the test is intended to isolate application logic.

quiz.question: What is the primary goal of a unit test?
quiz.explanation: Unit tests focus on small behavior without requiring the full system.

summary: A useful unit test names the behavior and fails for a meaningful reason.

lessons.title: MVC Testing, Integration Testing, and Debugging
lessons.description: Combine web-layer tests, real-database integration testing, and evidence-driven debugging.
learningObjectives: test controller contracts with MVC support
use Testcontainers when database fidelity matters
turn reproducible bugs into regression tests

notes.text: Test layers

items: Unit: isolated application behavior.
MVC/API: binding, validation, authorization and response contracts.
Integration: real persistence or infrastructure behavior.

notes.text:
mockMvc.perform(post("/api/issues")
    .contentType(MediaType.APPLICATION_JSON)
    .content("{"title":"","description":"Details","priority":"MEDIUM"}"))
    .andExpect(status().isBadRequest());
Testcontainers can supply disposable PostgreSQL instances for database integration tests, reducing the mismatch between an in-memory test database and production PostgreSQL.

practicals.title: Write an MVC Regression Test
practicals.description: Create an HTTP-level regression test for blank issue titles.
steps: Use Spring Boot MVC test support.
Verify the creation service is not called.
practicals.output: The test proves the validation contract at the controller boundary.

quiz.question: What does Testcontainers provide for a database integration test?
quiz.explanation: Testcontainers can start containerized infrastructure for tests.

summary: Debugging should follow reproduce → observe → hypothesize → test → fix → regress.

tasks.title: Diagnose a Database-Fidelity Failure
tasks.description: Repair a test that passes against an in-memory database but fails against PostgreSQL.
tasks.problemStatement: Move the database-dependent verification to a disposable PostgreSQL integration environment.
constraints: Do not weaken the production query just to satisfy a fake database.
tasks.hint: When SQL behavior is database-specific, test the same database family.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The test moves infrastructure-dependent verification onto a disposable PostgreSQL instance instead of assuming that an in-memory database behaves identically.

modules.title: Operations and Delivery
modules.description: Apply health monitoring, runtime configuration, container thinking, CI/CD, and deployment recovery practices.

lessons.title: Actuator Health and Operational Boundaries
lessons.description: Expose operational health without creating a broad information disclosure surface.
learningObjectives: explain why management exposure is constrained

notes.text: Health surface
Actuator provides production-oriented monitoring endpoints. Expose only the endpoints required by the environment and protect management interfaces appropriately.

practicals.title: Expose a Narrow Health Surface
practicals.description: Expose only the health endpoint in the learning configuration.
steps: Document why unrelated management endpoints remain closed.
practicals.solution:
management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health
practicals.output: The health endpoint is exposed while other actuator endpoints remain unexposed through this setting.

quiz.question: What does /actuator/health communicate?
quiz.explanation: The health endpoint reports application health state.

summary: Operational endpoints should be useful to operators and narrow enough to reduce information exposure.

lessons.title: Containers, CI/CD, and Rollback
lessons.description: Package the application as a deployable artifact and design a reproducible delivery path.

notes.text: Delivery

items: Build and test in CI.
Produce a versioned artifact only when quality gates pass.
Inject runtime configuration outside the artifact.
Keep a known-good artifact for rollback.

notes.text:
mvn clean verify
docker build -t issue-tracker:1.0.0 .

quiz.question: Why should CI commands be reproducible locally?
quiz.explanation: Reproducibility shortens the path from failure to diagnosis.

summary: Deployment quality is part of web engineering because a correct source tree must become a correctly configured running service.

tasks.title: Create an Operational Health Gate
tasks.description: Expose a narrow Actuator health endpoint and define a CI check for it.
tasks.problemStatement: Make /actuator/health available while avoiding broad management exposure.
constraints: Do not expose every management endpoint by default.
tasks.hint: Use the smallest management surface needed.
tasks.solutionCode:
management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health
tasks.solutionExplanation: The configuration limits the HTTP management surface to health for the learning environment. Production access control should still be designed at the deployment boundary.

modules.assessment: Explain the path from source commit to monitored deployment.

modules.title: Performance, Maintainability, and API Documentation
modules.description: Strengthen engineering judgment around concurrency, bounded work, and maintainable contracts.

lessons.title: Concurrency and Shared State
lessons.description: Recognize concurrency hazards in singleton Spring beans and reason about safe state.

notes.text: Concurrency model

Servlet applications may handle concurrent requests. Singleton beans are shared, so mutable instance fields can become race-prone or leak state across users. Keep request-specific state local to the request and use synchronization or concurrency-safe structures only when justified.

quiz.question: Why is mutable per-request state in a singleton bean dangerous?
quiz.explanation: Singleton beans are shared between concurrent requests.

summary: Concurrency safety is mostly about controlling shared mutable state and bounding resource use.

lessons.title: API Documentation and Maintainability
lessons.description: Document contracts and review code for clarity, boundaries, and safe change.

notes.text: Maintainability

items: Document the endpoint contract.
Document which roles can perform sensitive actions.
Prefer cohesive classes.
Keep security and validation expectations discoverable.

practicals.title: Document a Protected API
practicals.description: Write a contract for issue listing and creation.
steps: Document pagination and supported status filtering.
practicals.solution:
GET /api/issues?page=0&size=20
POST /api/issues
Success: 201 Created
Invalid input: 400 Bad Request
Unauthenticated: 401 Unauthorized
Forbidden operation: 403 Forbidden
practicals.output: The contract becomes a reference for clients and tests.

quiz.question: What should protected API documentation state?
quiz.explanation: Security requirements are part of the API contract.

summary: Clear contracts, focused classes, and regression tests make future changes safer.

tasks.title: Refactor a Mixed-Responsibility Controller
tasks.description: Review a controller that handles HTTP, business logic, SQL, and logging in one class.
tasks.problemStatement: Separate responsibilities without changing the public endpoint contract.
objectives: move business logic into a service
constraints: Preserve status codes and response semantics.
tasks.hint: Ask which lines would still exist if HTTP were replaced.
tasks.solutionExplanation: The refactored controller is responsible for transport concerns only. Service logic and persistence are injected behind explicit boundaries, improving reviewability and testability.

modules.assessment: Review an implementation for shared-state and contract risks.

modules.title: Final Project: Secure Issue Tracker
modules.description: Deliver the one integrated capstone and no separate module tasks.

lessons.title: Capstone Delivery and Engineering Walkthrough
lessons.description: Deliver the capstone and explain its technical and security decisions.

notes.text: Final walkthrough

A strong capstone is an integrated engineering system. The intern should demonstrate the application, run its tests, show validation and authorization behavior, explain the PostgreSQL schema, and describe deployment and rollback.
The capstone is training material and a practical assessment. It is not a guarantee of production readiness, employment, or accreditation.

quiz.question: What distinguishes a capstone from isolated exercises?
options: One coherent system integrating the taught competencies
quiz.answer: One coherent system integrating the taught competencies
quiz.explanation: The capstone demonstrates integrated engineering ability.

summary: The capstone is evaluated by implementation evidence and technical reasoning, not file count.

modules.assessment: Final capstone evaluation with engineering walkthrough.

project.heading: Build a Secure Production-Style Issue Tracking Web Application
project.description: Build one modular Java web application for a small engineering team to record and track software issues. The system combines Spring MVC, PostgreSQL persistence, Flyway migrations, Spring Data JPA, validation, Spring Security, server-rendered HTML, automated tests, operational health checks, and externalized configuration. It is intentionally a modular monolith so the intern can demonstrate the complete web-to-database path without unnecessary distributed-system infrastructure.
project.problemStatement: The team needs a central issue tracker where authenticated users can browse and create issues, while administrators can perform destructive actions. The application must reject malformed input, keep credentials protected, provide predictable error responses, and remain testable and deployable with external configuration.

functional: Authenticated users can list issues with pagination and optional status filtering.
Authenticated users can create issues with validated title, description, and priority.
Authenticated users can change issue status.
Only ADMIN users can delete issues.
The browser page renders issue data safely.
technical: Spring Boot 4.1.1, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Spring Security, Thymeleaf, Validation, Actuator.
JUnit 5/Spring test support and an optional Testcontainers integration layer.
security: Actuator exposure is limited to health in the sample configuration.
The browser uses DOM text insertion rather than raw HTML injection.
testing: Additional PostgreSQL integration tests using Testcontainers are recommended for the intern to add.
deployment: Inject secrets and configuration through deployment environment.
Retain a known-good build for rollback.

features: Paginated authenticated issue listing with optional OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/RESOLVED status filter.
Validated issue creation endpoint returning 201 Created on successful creation.
Status transition endpoint using a closed enum of allowed states.
ADMIN-only deletion enforced with @PreAuthorize at the server method boundary.
Centralized validation and not-found errors using ProblemDetail.
PostgreSQL schema with uniqueness, foreign-key, CHECK constraints, and status/created_at index.
Actuator health endpoint with narrow exposure.

technologyStack.name: Java 25
technologyStack.why: Current LTS Java release verified in Oracle's support roadmap.

technologyStack.name: Spring Boot 4.1.1
technologyStack.role: Bootstraps and auto-configures the web service
technologyStack.why: Current stable Boot release verified from Spring documentation.

technologyStack.name: Spring Security
technologyStack.why: Official security framework for Spring applications.

technologyStack.name: Spring Data JPA
technologyStack.why: Provides repository abstractions for Jakarta Persistence.

technologyStack.name: PostgreSQL
technologyStack.why: Mature relational database with strong constraints and query planning.

technologyStack.name: Flyway
technologyStack.why: Keeps schema changes repeatable and reviewable.

technologyStack.name: JUnit 5
technologyStack.why: Modern Jupiter test support in the Spring Boot test stack.

project.architecture: Browser/API client → Spring Security filters → DispatcherServlet → Controller → Service → Spring Data JPA repository → PostgreSQL. Flyway controls schema evolution. DTOs form HTTP contracts. Actuator provides a narrow health surface.
project.dataFlow: User → HTTPS/HTTP request at deployment edge → authentication/authorization → request validation → controller → transactional service → repository → PostgreSQL → DTO mapping → HTTP response → browser/API client.
implementationSteps: Install JDK 25, Maven, PostgreSQL, and Docker if you plan to run Testcontainers or containerize the application.
Create the Maven project and add the dependencies from pom.xml.
Create the Java package structure and main application class.
Create user and issue entities with explicit constraints and a creator foreign key.
Add the Flyway migration and keep Hibernate ddl-auto=validate so schema drift fails fast.
Create repositories for user lookup and paginated issue access.
Implement CustomUserDetailsService and PasswordEncoder-based credentials.
Configure Spring Security form login, request authentication, method authorization, and leave CSRF protection enabled.
Create request/response DTOs with validation.
Implement IssueService transaction boundaries and issue operations.
Implement REST endpoints for listing, creating, changing status, and deleting.
Add centralized ProblemDetail error handling.
Add the Thymeleaf login and issue-list views and safe client-side DOM rendering.
Set DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_USERNAME, DATABASE_PASSWORD, APP_ADMIN_PASSWORD, and APP_USER_PASSWORD at runtime.
Run mvn clean verify and add more PostgreSQL integration coverage with Testcontainers where Docker is available.
Run the application against PostgreSQL and verify login, create, list, status change, and admin delete.
Request /actuator/health and confirm only the intended management surface is exposed.
Build and document the deployable artifact, runtime configuration, monitoring, and rollback plan.

software: Docker optional for integration testing and container packaging
setupInstructions.database: Create an issue_tracker database and a database principal with only the permissions needed by the application. Do not use a PostgreSQL superuser credential in production.

howItWorks.startup: Spring Boot creates the servlet application context, Flyway applies V1, Hibernate validates the schema, and the initializer creates local users using runtime passwords.
howItWorks.authentication: Spring Security uses CustomUserDetailsService to load an encoded password and role from PostgreSQL. PasswordEncoder verifies the submitted password.
howItWorks.authorization: Authenticated application routes require identity; the DELETE operation additionally requires ADMIN via @PreAuthorize.
howItWorks.request: A controller accepts validated JSON, invokes a transactional service, the repository reads/writes PostgreSQL, and the service maps the entity to an IssueResponse DTO.
howItWorks.browser: The login page posts to Spring Security. The issue-list page fetches JSON and writes values with textContent, avoiding direct HTML injection.
howItWorks.testing: Unit tests isolate service behavior; MVC tests validate request contracts; security tests validate role enforcement. A full project extension should add Testcontainers-based PostgreSQL integration tests.
howItWorks.deployment: Maven produces the JAR. Deployment supplies database settings and secrets separately, exposes the application port, restricts management endpoints, and retains a known-good artifact for rollback.

securityReview: PasswordEncoder hashes passwords instead of persisting plaintext.
No credentials are stored in source code; runtime environment variables supply local passwords.
Database access uses JPA repository binding rather than string-built SQL from user input.
ProblemDetail error responses avoid stack traces.
Browser rendering uses textContent instead of innerHTML for API data.
Actuator exposes health only in the sample configuration.
CSRF remains enabled for the stateful browser security model.
performanceReview: The schema contains an index aligned with status filtering and created_at ordering.
Open EntityManager in View is disabled.
Query performance decisions should use EXPLAIN ANALYZE on representative data.
No unbounded application cache is introduced.
deploymentReview: Terminate HTTPS at the deployment edge or configure TLS according to the hosting platform.
Use external PostgreSQL and protect database connectivity.
Inject secrets through deployment secret management.
Restrict actuator endpoints and network access.
Monitor application health and database availability.
Test database backup and restore separately from application rollback.

troubleshooting.cause: The initializer intentionally refuses to create local users without runtime credentials.
troubleshooting.action: Set the required environment variables before startup.

troubleshooting.cause: The database migration history or target schema is inconsistent.
troubleshooting.action: Inspect Flyway state and fix migration/history deliberately rather than enabling Hibernate update.

project.explanation: The capstone integrates the internship as an engineering system rather than a set of isolated exercises. It has clear transport, business, and persistence boundaries; explicit relational constraints; versioned schema migration; browser authentication; server-side authorization; automated tests; and operational health. The architecture is deliberately a modular monolith to keep the web-to-database path understandable while still requiring real engineering judgment.
project.testingInstructions: Run `mvn clean verify`. If Docker is available, extend the suite with a Testcontainers PostgreSQL integration test and run it in CI. A passing local unit suite does not prove deployment correctness.
project.deploymentNotes: The supplied project is a training capstone, not a claim of production readiness for any specific organization. Production deployment must adapt authentication policy, TLS termination, database backup, availability, secrets management, network controls, logging, monitoring, and rollback to the actual environment.

finalProject.heading: Build a Secure Production-Style Issue Tracking Web Application
finalProject.description: Build one modular Java web application for a small engineering team to record and track software issues. The system combines Spring MVC, PostgreSQL persistence, Flyway migrations, Spring Data JPA, validation, Spring Security, server-rendered HTML, automated tests, operational health checks, and externalized configuration. It is intentionally a modular monolith so the intern can demonstrate the complete web-to-database path without unnecessary distributed-system infrastructure.
finalProject.problemStatement: The team needs a central issue tracker where authenticated users can browse and create issues, while administrators can perform destructive actions. The application must reject malformed input, keep credentials protected, provide predictable error responses, and remain testable and deployable with external configuration.

functional: Authenticated users can list issues with pagination and optional status filtering.
Authenticated users can create issues with validated title, description, and priority.
Authenticated users can change issue status.
Only ADMIN users can delete issues.
The browser page renders issue data safely.
technical: Spring Boot 4.1.1, Spring MVC, Spring Data JPA, Spring Security, Thymeleaf, Validation, Actuator.
JUnit 5/Spring test support and an optional Testcontainers integration layer.
security: Actuator exposure is limited to health in the sample configuration.
The browser uses DOM text insertion rather than raw HTML injection.
testing: Additional PostgreSQL integration tests using Testcontainers are recommended for the intern to add.
deployment: Inject secrets and configuration through deployment environment.
Retain a known-good build for rollback.

features: Paginated authenticated issue listing with optional OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/RESOLVED status filter.
Validated issue creation endpoint returning 201 Created on successful creation.
Status transition endpoint using a closed enum of allowed states.
ADMIN-only deletion enforced with @PreAuthorize at the server method boundary.
Centralized validation and not-found errors using ProblemDetail.
PostgreSQL schema with uniqueness, foreign-key, CHECK constraints, and status/created_at index.
Actuator health endpoint with narrow exposure.

finalProject.architecture: Browser/API client → Spring Security filters → DispatcherServlet → Controller → Service → Spring Data JPA repository → PostgreSQL. Flyway controls schema evolution. DTOs form HTTP contracts. Actuator provides a narrow health surface.
finalProject.dataFlow: User → HTTPS/HTTP request at deployment edge → authentication/authorization → request validation → controller → transactional service → repository → PostgreSQL → DTO mapping → HTTP response → browser/API client.
implementationSteps: Install JDK 25, Maven, PostgreSQL, and Docker if you plan to run Testcontainers or containerize the application.
Create the Maven project and add the dependencies from pom.xml.
Create the Java package structure and main application class.
Create user and issue entities with explicit constraints and a creator foreign key.
Add the Flyway migration and keep Hibernate ddl-auto=validate so schema drift fails fast.
Create repositories for user lookup and paginated issue access.
Implement CustomUserDetailsService and PasswordEncoder-based credentials.
Configure Spring Security form login, request authentication, method authorization, and leave CSRF protection enabled.
Create request/response DTOs with validation.
Implement IssueService transaction boundaries and issue operations.
Implement REST endpoints for listing, creating, changing status, and deleting.
Add centralized ProblemDetail error handling.
Add the Thymeleaf login and issue-list views and safe client-side DOM rendering.
Set DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_USERNAME, DATABASE_PASSWORD, APP_ADMIN_PASSWORD, and APP_USER_PASSWORD at runtime.
Run mvn clean verify and add more PostgreSQL integration coverage with Testcontainers where Docker is available.
Run the application against PostgreSQL and verify login, create, list, status change, and admin delete.
Request /actuator/health and confirm only the intended management surface is exposed.
Build and document the deployable artifact, runtime configuration, monitoring, and rollback plan.

software: Docker optional for integration testing and container packaging
setupInstructions.database: Create an issue_tracker database and a database principal with only the permissions needed by the application. Do not use a PostgreSQL superuser credential in production.

howItWorks.startup: Spring Boot creates the servlet application context, Flyway applies V1, Hibernate validates the schema, and the initializer creates local users using runtime passwords.
howItWorks.authentication: Spring Security uses CustomUserDetailsService to load an encoded password and role from PostgreSQL. PasswordEncoder verifies the submitted password.
howItWorks.authorization: Authenticated application routes require identity; the DELETE operation additionally requires ADMIN via @PreAuthorize.
howItWorks.request: A controller accepts validated JSON, invokes a transactional service, the repository reads/writes PostgreSQL, and the service maps the entity to an IssueResponse DTO.
howItWorks.browser: The login page posts to Spring Security. The issue-list page fetches JSON and writes values with textContent, avoiding direct HTML injection.
howItWorks.testing: Unit tests isolate service behavior; MVC tests validate request contracts; security tests validate role enforcement. A full project extension should add Testcontainers-based PostgreSQL integration tests.
howItWorks.deployment: Maven produces the JAR. Deployment supplies database settings and secrets separately, exposes the application port, restricts management endpoints, and retains a known-good artifact for rollback.

securityReview: PasswordEncoder hashes passwords instead of persisting plaintext.
No credentials are stored in source code; runtime environment variables supply local passwords.
Database access uses JPA repository binding rather than string-built SQL from user input.
ProblemDetail error responses avoid stack traces.
Browser rendering uses textContent instead of innerHTML for API data.
Actuator exposes health only in the sample configuration.
CSRF remains enabled for the stateful browser security model.
performanceReview: The schema contains an index aligned with status filtering and created_at ordering.
Open EntityManager in View is disabled.
Query performance decisions should use EXPLAIN ANALYZE on representative data.
No unbounded application cache is introduced.
deploymentReview: Terminate HTTPS at the deployment edge or configure TLS according to the hosting platform.
Use external PostgreSQL and protect database connectivity.
Inject secrets through deployment secret management.
Restrict actuator endpoints and network access.
Monitor application health and database availability.
Test database backup and restore separately from application rollback.

troubleshooting.cause: The initializer intentionally refuses to create local users without runtime credentials.
troubleshooting.action: Set the required environment variables before startup.

troubleshooting.cause: The database migration history or target schema is inconsistent.
troubleshooting.action: Inspect Flyway state and fix migration/history deliberately rather than enabling Hibernate update.
Use an authorized administrator account when testing the destructive operation.
